title: Same Tree
description: Given the roots of two binary trees `p` and `q`, return `true` if they have exactly the same structure and every pair of corresponding nodes holds the same value. Otherwise return `false`.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each tree <= 100
hints: Compare the two trees node by node, walking them in lockstep.
What should happen when both nodes are empty? When only one is?
If both are empty return true; if exactly one is empty or the values differ return false; otherwise both left pairs and both right pairs must match.

solution.explanation: Walk both trees together. If both nodes are empty they match; if only one is empty or the values differ, they do not; otherwise the trees match exactly when the left subtrees match and the right subtrees match. Each pair of nodes is visited at most once, so time is O(n) and the recursion stack uses O(h) space.
